title: Five-pillar building and zakah questions
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y7 lesson 10 (Pupil PDF worksheet: five-pillar building and zakah questions)
intro: Lesson 10: Islam is built on five: the hadith of the five pillars. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Pillar
What it is
Key fact
rows: Declaring Allah is One and Muhammad ﷺ His Messenger
The foundation of all the others
Connects the believer to Allah through the day
Once in a life, if able (3:97)

model.title: Aminah has £4,000 savings, above the nisab, for a full lunar year. How much zakah does she pay?

box.title: Draw a building with five pillars (no people). On each pillar: its name, what it involves, how it helps the community.

keywords.def: pillars: the main supports of Islam
obligatory charity, 2.5% of savings above the nisab
the minimum amount of wealth before zakah is due
pilgrimage to Makkah, once in a lifetime for those able

questions.q: Calculate the zakah on £2,000 of savings held above the nisab for a lunar year.
Who narrated 'Islam is built on five'?
Which pillar is once in a lifetime for those able?
Draw a labelled building with five pillars (no people). On each pillar write its name, what it involves and how it helps the community. Pupil PDF or drawing tablet.
questions.a: Five correct pillars in the hadith's order, each with a correct description and a community benefit.

questions.q: Extend: calculate zakah on £6,400 above the nisab.
Stretch: why do you think fasting and Hajj are in a different order in another narration?
questions.a: Narrators reported the pillars in different orders; both are authentic and the order does not change the obligation.

questions.q: In the hadith, which pillar is the foundation the others rest on?
questions.a: A) The shahadah. The shahadah comes first: without belief in tawheed and the Messenger the other acts are not accepted as Islam.

questions.q: What percentage is zakah on savings?
Think again: what happens if a pillar is removed?
questions.a: The building is weakened; neglecting a pillar weakens a Muslim's Islam.
